Sudan

A long history of gold mining, with opportunities that begin with careful geological and operational assessment.

COUNTRY OVERVIEW

Mining at a glance.

Key minerals
Gold · Chromite · Industrial minerals
Geographic focus
Red Sea Hills · Northern Sudan
01 / GOLD

Gold in Sudan.

Gold is Sudan’s leading mineral export by value. Artisanal mining accounts for much of its output, alongside organised mining operations. The Red Sea Hills and northern desert form part of the country’s established gold exploration landscape.

02 / MINING

The wider mining sector.

Sudan also produces chromite, gypsum, salt and other industrial minerals. Geological work, sampling and reliable site information are essential to understanding individual deposits.

03 / OPPORTUNITIES

Where to explore potential.

Areas for technical assessment, subject to site verification and feasibility.

01

Gold exploration

Review historic workings and geological records to identify targets for mapping and sampling, where safe access is possible.

02

Technical assessment

Assess sampling quality, mineral processing options and operating conditions before planning further development.

03

Responsible sourcing

Evaluate traceability and working practices with verified local partners before considering a supply relationship.

Before moving forward

Conflict affects access, logistics and gold supply chains. Any proposed work needs a current security assessment, verified counterparties and responsible sourcing checks before field activity is considered.
